subject: Tiered rollforward extension plan and surge capacity — next steps
messages:
From: Ellie Stevens <ellie.stevens@brightretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@brightretail.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window — proposal to rollforward & tiered extension

Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’ve finished internal planning and want to propose a different approach for our upcoming renewal: instead of a simple annual renewal, we’d like a 2-year extension with a staged (tiered) rollforward so we can absorb a marketing-driven jump toward the end of Q1. High level: year 1 baseline + 40% committed uplift in month 10, year 2 baseline with optional auto-rollover at agreed floor.

We need answers on:
- Can you support a ramp trigger (usage-based) that moves capacity earlier if actual consumption hits the trigger?
- Billing: will BrightRetail be billed on committed tokens or actual usage with a true-up?
- Any impact on pricing if we set a firm floor for year 2 and allow automatic rollover at floor + 10%?

I’ve attached our rough forecast. Also looping in contracts for timing. We’re hoping to finalize commercial terms by Sept 23 to align with finance.

Appreciate a quick feasibility check and a proposed commercial sketch.

—Ellie

[Attachment: usage_forecast_Q4.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Stevens <ellie.stevens@brightretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — proposal to rollforward & tiered extension

Thanks Ellie — this is doable and we can sketch a short playbook. Quick answers up front:
- Ramp trigger: yes, we can implement a usage-based trigger that opens burst capacity and promotes a partial commitment earlier (we call this a surge-trigger). We’ll define a clear threshold and activation window.
- Billing: typical structure is committed + overage true-up monthly; we can also do committed-only billing with quarterly true-ups if you prefer predictable invoicing.
- Year 2 floor: we can price year 2 at a negotiated floor and include an auto-rollover clause at floor + 10% with optional early-exit at a small break fee.

I’m attaching a redline sketch of terms and a sample SLA ramp activation flow. Karthik — can you review baseline pricing and margin impact? Lauren — need a note on invoicing cadence and whether finance is OK with the proposed quarterly true-up.

I’ll follow up with a cleaned contract draft by EOD Friday.

Best,
Mina
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: BR_Contract_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ellie Stevens <ellie.stevens@brightretail.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — proposal to rollforward & tiered extension

Mina / Ellie,

Reviewed the sketch — high level thumbs up. A few commercial guardrails to call out:
1) Surge-trigger: suggest a 3x 7-day lookback to avoid noisy spikes (trigger = 7-day rolling average >= 120% of baseline for 3 consecutive days). Activation moves BrightRetail to the next committed tier for a minimum 30-day period.
2) Billing cadence: recommend monthly invoicing with a quarterly committed true-up for ease of bookkeeping. Finance prefers clear committed floors rather than committed-only billing.
3) Year 2 floor discount: we can offer a 7.5% discount off list if BrightRetail commits to the floor and a 6-month notice for early-exit applies with a small termination fee (pro-rated).

If those sound acceptable, we’ll bake them into the draft. Also recommend adding a short paragraph on fallback model variants if a specific model is deprecated mid-term (to avoid service interruptions).

-Karthik

From: Ellie Stevens <ellie.stevens@brightretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@brightretail.com, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — proposal to rollforward & tiered extension

Thanks — that approach looks reasonable. A couple of counter-points from our side after legal review:
- Trigger sensitivity: can we shorten to a 2-day rolling average? Our marketing campaigns are short and intense; a longer lookback could delay needed capacity.
- Auto-rollover: request that auto-rollover require a 30-day notice window instead of automatic lock-in. We want a chance to re-evaluate if product direction changes.
- Pricing: suggest a 5% discount for committing to the year-2 floor (we prefer the lower discount and flexibility).

Contracts asked that you provide a sample DocuSign route and a final redline by COB Wednesday (Sept 22) so we can route internally. Appreciate the fast turn.

—Ellie

Ellie — thanks for the feedback. Attached is the final redline (highlights below) and the DocuSign route link. Summary of negotiated points: 
- Trigger sensitivity set to 2-day rolling average as requested, with a 48-hour debounce to avoid one-off blips. Activation still enforces a 30-day minimum on the promoted tier.
- Auto-rollover converted to auto-offer: BrightRetail will receive notice 30 days before the rollover; final acceptance required to lock year 2 terms.
- Pricing: we agreed to a 5% discount on year-2 floor.
- Billing: monthly invoices with quarterly committed true-up.
- Fallback models: we added a short compatibility clause and an automatic routing to closest-performing variant during deprecation windows.
